finding: Keeping the new replay/intent metadata under outer conversation-state version=2 is not rollback-safe. The exact current v2 loader reconstructs only the known ConversationSegment fields and ignores unknown top-level/per-record metadata; any later save serializes only those reconstructed fields. Therefore an older binary can silently erase replay_response/inflight/provider-intent safety evidence. Merely bumping the file to version=3 is also insufficient by itself: the exact current store marks an unsupported version persistence_blocked, but the exact current server does not gate provider entry on that blocked state and can continue to Notion with empty in-memory segment state.
required_invariant: Before any durable replay/provider-intent schema epoch is published, deploy a compatibility-floor server that checks persistence readiness after loading/get cleanup and fails before every provider-entering operation, including normal Responses and compaction, when the durable state schema is unsupported or blocked.

After that floor is established, the replay/intent schema may advance to a new outer state version (recommended version=3). New code may read legacy v2 conservatively and write v3 atomically; v2 records do not acquire replay safety retroactively and legacy exact retries remain fail-closed where evidence is missing.

Rollback must be bounded by an explicit minimum_safe_rollback_commit. Never roll back below the compatibility floor after a v3 state has been published. A floor-aware v2 binary encountering v3 must fail closed before provider access rather than treating state as an optimization.
Do not rely on unknown-field preservation while keeping version=2: the exact current loader/save pair does not preserve unknown replay/intent fields.
interaction_with_v12_v26: V12 originally kept STATE_VERSION=2 to avoid breaking the current loader. V22-V26 require durable pre-provider intents and exact replay metadata. V27 supersedes the compatibility assumption: safety metadata needs an explicit schema epoch plus a rollback floor; otherwise downgrade can erase the very evidence used to prevent duplicate provider planning/side effects.
